title: Checking the Evidence: A Study Group Talks About Flashcards · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: At the Westbridge Adult Learning Centre, four learners meet on Tuesday evenings. Their teacher, Ms. Chen, asked them to test a study method for three weeks. The method is simple: use flashcards for fifteen minutes every day. The group wants to know if the method works. They have collected their own data, and now they are discussing the evidence. “I have used flashcards since the first week,” says Marco. “I already know fifty new words. Before, I forgot words quickly. Now I remember them.” Lena disagrees. “I have not finished my flashcard set yet. I started late, so my numbers are low. But I have studied with a partner for two weeks, and that helps me more.” Ms. Chen shows a chart. “You have all improved since September. But please be careful. You have also changed other things. Marco, you have read a short news story every morning since week two.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you use flashcards to study English?
How long have you studied English?
Have you ever studied with a partner?
What do you do when you forget a new word?

Part 2
Describe a study method you have tried. You should say: what the method was; when you started it; how long you have used it; and whether it has helped you.

Part 3
Why do some people prefer studying alone?
How can learners check if a study method really works?
Have study habits changed in your country in recent years?
Is it better to study for a short time every day or for a long time once a week?
